# Path-based allowlist for `validate_pool.py` privacy scan.
# One pattern per line. A file is exempted if its path (with both / and \ separators)
# contains any non-comment line below as a substring. Lines starting with `#` and
# blank lines are ignored.
#
# Use this only for files that legitimately contain example credentials, hashes,
# or terms in documentation/teaching contexts. Real leaks must be removed,
# never allowlisted.

# --- Legitimate documentation / teaching examples ---
# Paths are written without a leading `.github/` so they match both the
# canonical pool layout and the runtime-exported `.codex/` mirror.
instructions/security.instructions.md

instructions/github-actions.instructions.md
agents/security-analyst.agent.md

skills/cloud/building-mcp-server-on-cloudflare/references/oauth-setup.md
skills/devops/ci-cd-pipeline/SKILL.md
skills/frontend/brand-design/SKILL.md
skills/productivity/jira-issues/SKILL.md
skills/testing/playwright/lib/helpers.js

# --- windows-deployment: generic Windows deploy skill; vmie- is the example NSSM service-naming convention (org prefix), not a secret ---
skills/devops/windows-deployment/SKILL.md

# --- Pool documentation referencing itself ---
agent-docs/agent-workflow-design-reference.md
agent-docs/PROJECT-ONBOARDING-RUNBOOK.md

# --- Remediation plan deliberately enumerates leaked tokens for cleanup tracking ---
plans/2026-04-27-ai-resource-pool-remediation.md

litellm.config.example.yaml

# --- Wallchart system documentation — vmie- refers to NSSM service naming convention, not a credential ---
agent-docs/WORKFLOW-WALLCHART.md

# --- Flattened plugin-bundle dist paths (flatten_skills drops the category dir, so
# skills/<category>/<name>/ becomes skills/<name>/). The --include-dist scan walks the
# exported bundles, so each allowlisted skill above also needs its category-less form here.
# All entries below mirror an already-vetted source entry (example credentials in teaching
# docs, or the intentional vmie- naming convention). ---

# --- The allowlist file itself documents the vmie- substring in comments; exempt it so the
# --include-dist scan of mirror copies doesn't flag its own documentation. ---
tools/pool-validator/denylist-exceptions.txt

# --- The privacy mechanism itself (added 2026-08-05 with the tracked-file scan) ---
# These files contain internal markers BY DESIGN: they are the regression guards that
# assert the denylist still detects them. Scrubbing them would silently disable the very
# protection that stops internal hostnames reaching a public repo — the check must not
# eat its own tests. validate_pool.py itself is excluded in code, not here.
scripts/tests/test_validate_pool.py
scripts/tests/test_sync_ps1.py
scripts/tests/test_check_doc_coverage.py
